newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil portworkers threaten to strike over wages.
newsitem.headline: Brazil portworkers threaten to strike over wages.

text.p: Brazilian administrative portworkers are threatening to go on national strike on August 11 unless Transport Minister Eliseu Padilha awards them a collective wage rise of 15.52 percent, a union official said.

"If the minister does not reply or his reply is negative, the strike starts on August 11 for an indefinite period," said Jose Horatio Freitas, administrative and financial secretary of the National Portworkers' Union.

The transport minister has until July 31 to make a decision, Freitas said. Administrative portworkers are demanding that the wage rise be made retroactive to June 1 and also want guarantees they will retain their jobs, he added.
A national schedule tentatively scheduled for July 14 was averted because Padilha agreed in a document sent to unions Monday to negotiate a new collective wage agreement for 1997, Freitas said.
Even though unions have already decided to go ahead with the August 11 strike should their demands not be met, they could accept a government counter-porposal, Freitas said.
"If there were a counter-proposal, we would call the unions and they would decide," he said.
